question.:question/problem:
Consider the following system of equations.

$$
\left\{\begin{aligned}2x-4y &=4 \\ -4x+6y &=15 \\ -10x+2y &=37\end{aligned}\right.
$$

Which of the following statements are true?

Select all that apply.
question.:question/worked-solution:
To classify the system, we first need to find its solution. The augmented matrix for this system is

$$
M=\left[\begin{array}{cc|c}2 & -4 & 4 \\ -4 & 6 & 15 \\ -10 & 2 & 37\end{array}\right].
$$

Using the method of Gaussian elimination, we can reduce this matrix to row echelon form as follows:

$$
\begin{aligned}M & =\left[\begin{array}{cc|c}2 & -4 & 4 \\ -4 & 6 & 15 \\ -10 & 2 & 37\end{array}\right] & {R}_{2} & :={R}_{2}+2{R}_{1} \\  & ∼\left[\begin{array}{cc|c}2 & -4 & 4 \\ 0 & -2 & 23 \\ -10 & 2 & 37\end{array}\right] & {R}_{3} & :={R}_{3}+5{R}_{1} \\  & ∼\left[\begin{array}{cc|c}2 & -4 & 4 \\ 0 & -2 & 23 \\ 0 & -18 & 57\end{array}\right] & {R}_{3} & :={R}_{3}+(-9){R}_{2} \\  & ∼\left[\begin{array}{cc|c}2 & -4 & 4 \\ 0 & -2 & 23 \\ 0 & 0 & -150\end{array}\right]\end{aligned}
$$

The final row corresponds to the equation $0x+0y=-150,$ and this has no solution. Therefore, our system has no solution, and we conclude that the system is inconsistent.

As a result, only statement “The system is inconsistent” is true.

:question/answer-fields.:answer-field/key: The system has a unique solution

question.:question/problem:
Consider the following system of equations

$$
\left\{\begin{aligned}-4x-6y &=-11 \\ -2x+4y &=3 \\ 2x+10y &=14.\end{aligned}\right.
$$

Which of the following statements are true?

Select all that apply.
question.:question/worked-solution:
To classify the system, we first try to find its solution. The augmented matrix for this system is 

$$
M=\left[\begin{array}{cc|c}-4 & -6 & -11 \\ -2 & 4 & 3 \\ 2 & 10 & 14\end{array}\right].
$$

Using the method of Gaussian elimination, we can reduce this matrix to row echelon form as follows:

$$
\begin{aligned}M & =\left[\begin{array}{cc|c}-4 & -6 & -11 \\ -2 & 4 & 3 \\ 2 & 10 & 14\end{array}\right] & {R}_{1} & ↔{R}_{2} \\  & ∼\left[\begin{array}{cc|c}-2 & 4 & 3 \\ -4 & -6 & -11 \\ 2 & 10 & 14\end{array}\right] & {R}_{2} & :={R}_{2}+(-2){R}_{1} \\  & ∼\left[\begin{array}{cc|c}-2 & 4 & 3 \\ 0 & -14 & -17 \\ 2 & 10 & 14\end{array}\right] & {R}_{3} & :={R}_{3}+{R}_{1} \\  & ∼\left[\begin{array}{cc|c}-2 & 4 & 3 \\ 0 & -14 & -17 \\ 0 & 14 & 17\end{array}\right] & {R}_{3} & :={R}_{3}+{R}_{2} \\  & ∼\left[\begin{array}{cc|c}-2 & 4 & 3 \\ 0 & -14 & -17 \\ 0 & 0 & 0\end{array}\right]\end{aligned}
$$

 

Since any numbers $x$ and $y$ are solutions to the third equation $0x+0y=0$, we can remove this equation from the system. So, the corresponding system is now

$$
\left\{\begin{aligned}-2x+4y &=3 \\ -14y &=-17.\end{aligned}\right.
$$

From the second equation, we get $y=\frac{17}{14}.$ Substituting this into the first equation, we get

$$
-2x+4\left(\frac{17}{14}\right)=3\,⟹\,x=\frac{13}{14}.
$$

 
So, we conclude that the system is consistent independent. 

As a result, only statement “The system is consistent independent” is true.
